doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Scat singing jump tunes with Harry James
summary: Palmer sang the rhythm numbers Sinatra did not, sings a snippet of Sunny Side of the Street, and describes how James called tunes.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well you’re listed in this picture with the Harry James band from 1939, in addition to trumpet, as a singer also.
Well I used to do what they call scat singing.
Scat vocals. I sang the songs that Frank didn’t want to sing. No they were the rhythm songs really.
The jump tunes, yeah, where you didn’t sing ballad style you know. So that’s what I sang.
Like give me an example of one of the jump tunes you might have sung.
Gee, I couldn’t off hand, really. I can’t really.
Kind of like “Sunny Side of the Street?”

I can’t even remember how that goes — “Sunny Side of the Street.” [sings] Get your hat/get your coat/leave your worries on your doorstep/life is oh so sweet/on the sunny side of the street. Get your hat, your cane, your coat, your gloves/leave your worries on your doorstep baby.
Would Harry James call those tunes out when the crowd was really getting — was he working the crowd kind of?

Yeah. We didn’t know what went on in his mind. We just, whatever he called out we took out tunes and sometimes we just, I would know like what followed, his general pattern, so sometimes I’d just have it stuck up so I could reach it quickly you know.
